ety.text: Inherited from Middle English lid, lyd, from Old English hlid, from Proto-West Germanic *hlid, from Proto-Germanic *hlidą (compare Dutch lid, German Lid (“eyelid”), Swedish lid (“gate”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlitós (“covered”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱley- (“to cover”).

senses.d: The top or cover of a container.

ex: Mal rider, shortboard or lid everyone surfs like a kook sometimes.
the rest of us managed to dodge out of control lid riders

senses.d: An operculum or other lid-like cover.
In amateur radio, an incompetent operator.
A hermetically sealed top piece on a microchip such as the integrated heat spreader on a CPU.
A restraint or control, as when "putting a lid" on something.
A kid (from the rhyming slang bin lid).

grp.label: to put a lid on something

ety.text: Inherited from Old French covercle, from Latin cooperculum.
From Vulgar Latin *coperclum, from Latin cooperculum, from cooperiō.
From Frankish *tappo, from Proto-Germanic *tappô (“plug, tap”). Doublet of zaffo.

es:tapa.gl: lid, cap (the top or cover of a container)
